Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 years)  
Patient: Itha (26 y, female) – Telehealth consultation

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  
  • 4-day history of dry, red, itchy skin on arms and hands, began after swimming in chlorinated pool; coconut butter ineffective.  
  • Reports work-related stress and fatigue; otherwise well, no fever, vomiting, diarrhea, or systemic symptoms.

- Relevant family medical history:  
  • Father – asthma.  
  • Mother – hay fever.  
  • No known family skin disorders.

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  
  • Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive pill) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Coconut butter (topical moisturiser, OTC) – frequency not documented.  
  • No other regular or PRN medicines.

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.

- Sexual and reproductive health:  
  • Uses combined oral contraceptive pill.  
  • No further sexual history recorded.

- Physical activity and nutrition:  
  • Swims recreationally; no other exercise pattern documented.  
  • Eats and drinks “as normal”; no dietary restrictions except possible lactose intolerance.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  
  • Non-smoker.  
  • Minimal alcohol intake (patient states “no” when asked if drinks much).  
  • Denies recreational drug use.

- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  
  • Work stress; feels tired.  
  • No screening for depression/anxiety or self-harm; risk not assessed.

- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  
  • Lives alone.  
  • Works as a primary school teacher; recent increased workload and stress.  
  • No caring responsibilities mentioned.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings:  
• Acute, localized pruritic erythematous dermatitis of arms/hands following chlorine exposure; no systemic symptoms; background atopy in family; work stress present.

Working diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis secondary to recent swimming (chlorine).  

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):  
1. Irritant contact dermatitis – High likelihood: acute onset after pool exposure; distribution on exposed skin; dry/red/itchy; no vesicles.  
2. Allergic contact dermatitis to chlorine/soap – Moderate likelihood: similar temporal link; immune-mediated reaction possible.  
3. Atopic dermatitis flare – Moderate likelihood: pruritic dry rash with family atopy and stress trigger, though no prior history.

Management priorities:  
• Symptom control (topical steroid, emollient, oral antihistamine).  
• Education about avoiding/limiting chlorine exposure, gentle skin care, stress management.  
• Safety-net advice: return if worsening or no improvement in one week.

Management Plan

- Prescribed/Recommended:  
  • Mild-moderate potency topical corticosteroid cream – dose/route/frequency not documented during call.  
  • Emollient moisturiser for frequent application.  
  • OTC oral antihistamine (e.g., loratadine or chlorphenamine) PRN for itch.  
  • Provided patient information leaflet on dermatitis.

- Follow-up: Review in 1 week if rash not improving or sooner if deteriorates.

- Patient education:  
  • Avoid prolonged chlorinated pool exposure; rinse skin promptly after swimming.  
  • Continue stress-reduction strategies; adequate rest and hydration.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded (stress noted but no referral arranged).  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Irritant contact dermatitis – High: Most plausible given acute onset after chlorine exposure and localized distribution.  
2. Allergic contact dermatitis – Moderate: Same temporal relationship; immune response possible though presentation lacks vesicles.  
3. Atopic dermatitis – Moderate: Supported by family atopy and stress trigger; less likely due to absence of prior episodes.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs (BP, pulse), height/weight/BMI, waist circumference, immunisation status, basic mental health screening, vision/hearing screening, urinalysis, cervical screening status, alcohol quantity, detailed exercise history.  
● No contradictions noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear, but limited to telehealth history; physical examination and objective data not obtained.
